skill.name: commit-helper
skill.description: Generates and validates Conventional Commit messages for the Logseq Template Graph project using staged git changes, project scopes, and commit templates.
skill.summary: Create accurate Conventional Commit messages from git changes and project-specific scopes.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many command patterns, but review found they are Markdown examples, inline Conventional Commit syntax, and copyable git commit snippets. The hardcoded URL is a public documentation link, and no prompt injection, hidden execution, network exfiltration, or reconnaissance intent was found.

remediation.issue: Copyable shell snippets may confuse automated scanners and cautious users.
remediation.suggestion: Show the commit message first, then provide the shell command as an optional user-run convenience.

remediation.issue: The skill asks the agent to inspect git status and diffs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep commands read-only unless the user explicitly asks to create a commit.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages takes time and requires consistent project rules. This skill reviews git changes and proposes Conventional Commit messages with the right type, scope, body, and footer.
actual_capabilities: Inspects staged and unstaged git changes when tool access is available.
Maps changed files to project-specific Conventional Commit types and scopes.
Generates concise subject lines, optional bodies, and breaking-change footers.
Validates commit messages for type, scope, imperative mood, length, and punctuation.
Provides simple, detailed, and breaking-change commit templates.
Explains why a suggested commit type and scope fit the detected changes.
limitations: Project scopes are tailored to the Logseq Template Graph repository.
It may need user context to understand intent beyond the visible diff.
It cannot verify issue numbers or pull request references without repository access.
Git command execution depends on the host tool permissions and user approval model.

use_cases.title: Prepare feature commits
use_cases.description: Turn staged feature changes into a clear Conventional Commit with the correct scope and optional body.

use_cases.title: Review release changes
use_cases.description: Identify breaking changes and create commit messages that include required migration notes.

use_cases.title: Standardize team history
use_cases.description: Check proposed messages against project rules before commits reach shared branches.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest one Conventional Commit message with a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare commit options
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my current changes and give three commit message options. Explain the type and scope tradeoffs for each option.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an existing message
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this commit message against the project rules. Suggest a corrected version if it has format, scope, or wording problems.

prompt_templates.title: Handle a breaking change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes for breaking behavior. Draft a Conventional Commit with a body, footer, and migration guidance if needed.

output_examples.input: Staged changes add a Recipe class, cooking properties, and documentation.
output_examples.output: Recommends a feature commit scoped to classes, with a body listing the new properties and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: A proposed message says: Added new class.
output_examples.output: Explains that the message is too vague and past tense, then suggests an imperative Conventional Commit subject.

output_examples.input: Staged changes remove a deprecated class and add migration notes.
output_examples.output: Flags the change as breaking and recommends a commit with a breaking-change footer and migration summary.

best_practices: Stage related changes before asking for a final commit message.
Share the purpose of the change when the diff alone does not show intent.
Review generated commit commands before running them in a shell.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated feature, fix, and documentation work in one commit.
Do not accept vague subjects such as update files or fix bug.
Do not mark breaking changes without a clear explanation and migration note.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It suggests commit messages and optional commands. The user decides whether to run them.

faq.question: Which commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the Conventional Commits format with project-specific scopes for Logseq Template Graph changes.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest the breaking-change marker, footer, and migration guidance when the diff shows breaking behavior.

faq.question: Does it require staged changes?
faq.answer: Staged changes are preferred for final messages. It can also inspect unstaged changes for planning.

faq.question: Can I use it outside the Logseq Template Graph project?
faq.answer: Yes, but some scopes and examples are project-specific and may need adjustment.

faq.question: What tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects access to git status and diff output through Claude, Codex, or Claude Code tool support.
